Mellifluous

meh-LIF-loo-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Mellifluous is sweet or musical to hear; smoothly and pleasantly flowing.

Audiences filled the hall for hours just to hear the soprano's mellifluous rendition of the old ballad.

Worked Example

The radio host's mellifluous voice made even the traffic report sound like a lullaby.

A voice that turns a dry traffic report into something soothing is exactly mellifluous.

How Mellifluous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

honeyed

honeyed: sweet-sounding, especially in speech

euphonious

euphonious: pleasant-sounding

Antonyms

cacophonous

cacophonous: harsh and grating in sound

How Strong Is It? — melodic → dulcet → mellifluous

melodic vs. mellifluous

melodic vs. mellifluous: Melodic simply means having a pleasant tune or rhythm, a common musical description; mellifluous specifically evokes a smooth, honey-like flow to a voice or sound.

dulcet vs. mellifluous

dulcet vs. mellifluous: Dulcet leans toward soft, soothing sweetness, almost lullaby-like, while mellifluous emphasizes the smooth, unbroken FLOW of the sound as much as its sweetness.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of mellifluous.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — mel

root — mel: honey (Latin)

root — flu

root — flu: to flow (Latin (fluere))

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Mellifluous combines Latin mel ('honey') + fluere ('to flow') + -ous -- literally 'flowing with honey,' describing sound as sweet as honey.

Use the root in a new word: fluent

Use the root in a new word: fluent: The same fluere root gives us the everyday word fluent -- both words describe something moving smoothly, without interruption, whether speech in general or a particularly sweet-sounding voice.

Word Choice

Mellifluous describes the smooth, sweet SOUND of a specific voice or piece of music, distinct from Euphony (taught earlier in this course), which is the more general noun for the pleasing quality of any sound, especially in language.
